changes: Split — the last piece of the Blackjack polish arc, now built and verified. Tracks a genuinely second, independent hand per seat rather than reworking the whole model around always-two-hands, the same "parallel track, only populated when actually used" approach single-player Blackjack itself takes for its own split.

New split action on the server, with the same value-match rule single-player uses (a Ten and a King can split together, not just exact rank matches). Hit and Stand both hand off between the two sub-hands within the same seat's own turn before moving on to the next seat. Double is blocked after a split, and a seat can only split once — same simplified rule set single-player already settled on.

Settlement now evaluates each sub-hand independently against the dealer. This was verified with two direct simulations before shipping, not just written and trusted: one confirming a split hand that wins one side and busts the other nets exactly zero, and a second confirming specifically that a split hand landing on 21 pays as a regular win, not a blackjack — both came back correct.

On the table itself: both hands now show side by side with a marker for whichever one is currently active, a Split button that only ever appears when splitting is actually legal, and the results panel breaks a split hand into its own two lines plus the combined total rather than a single outcome word that wouldn't mean anything for two separate hands.

Also fixed a real bug caught by an actual render before shipping, not assumed away: four action buttons at equal width didn't fit the row — Split was genuinely getting clipped at the edge. Switched to a percentage-based width so it wraps into a clean 2x2 grid instead.
